title: Teach the agent four conventions it cannot guess
goal: The repo follows four non-obvious conventions and has no context file. Write AGENTS.md (and a thin CLAUDE.md that imports it), then have the agent add an apply-discount handler that follows all four without you repeating them in the prompt.

starter_prompts.claude: Read src/ and test/. Write an AGENTS.md at the repo root with only what a new engineer could not guess from the code: the conventions, the test command and what done means. Keep it under 40 lines. Then create CLAUDE.md that contains just the line @AGENTS.md. Do not implement any feature yet. Afterwards run /context and tell me which memory files loaded.
starter_prompts.codex: Read src/ and test/. Write an AGENTS.md at the repo root with only what a new engineer could not guess from the code: the conventions, the test command and what done means. Keep it under 40 lines. Do not implement any feature yet. Then, in a new session, ask me for the feature.

solution_notes: AGENTS.md is the single source of truth. CLAUDE.md is two lines: an @AGENTS.md import plus one Claude-only note, so the tools cannot drift apart.

It lists only rules the code does not make obvious (integer cents and the Cents suffix, AppError codes, log.js instead of console, one kebab-case file per handler). It skips anything the agent can read from the code, such as the directory tree.
Every rule is concrete enough to check, and the test command and a definition of done are stated, so the agent can verify its own work.
The feature prompt in the solution is one line (add applyDiscount) and does not repeat any convention. The context file carries them.
